title: Throughput guardrails, soft-evacuation windows, and residency-aware routing for regional Dedicated pools
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Problem: Customers running Dedicated capacity across regions need predictable throughput guarantees while preserving data residency constraints and minimizing user-visible disruption during zone or regional evacuations. Current placement only supports coarse region affinity and blunt failover which causes short term overpressure on surviving zones and occasional residency violations for strict EU/APAC customers.

Goal: Implement a coordinated set of features: (1) per-fleet throughput guardrails and soft-evacuation windows that pre-warm and throttle traffic during planned and unplanned drains, (2) residency-aware routing policy that never routes EU-tagged requests outside permitted zones, and (3) an evacuation simulation harness + telemetry so SRE/product can validate SLOs under staged drains. This ticket implements the orchestration and policy layer plus a conservative rollout plan.

Non-goals: Reworking kernel-level batching optimizations or introducing new quantization modes (separate work). We will rely on existing KV cache and batching improvements as-is.
acceptance_criteria: Throughput guardrails: admin can set per-fleet min/reserved RPS and max burst credits; metrics reflect reservation utilization within 30s.

Soft-evacuation windows: initiating a zone drain triggers a configurable pre-drain window (default 120s) to pre-warm surviving nodes, and a staged ramp-down that limits new session placement to preserve throughput for existing sessions.
Residency routing: requests tagged with residency=europe or residency=apac are never routed to non-compliant zones; unit and integration tests cover routing decisions and policy fallbacks.
Failover SLOs: in our staged evacuation simulation, request loss <= 0.2% and p95 latency increase <= 20% at target throughput for a fleet with 50% cross-zone spare capacity configured.
Simulation harness: provides a dashboard and reproducible runbook (Confluence link) that SRE and PM can run before rollouts.
Rollback: feature can be toggled per-fleet and globally; rollback completes within 60s and observed traffic returns to pre-rollout routing behavior.
Docs & runbooks: Console UI docs, CLI flags, and an ops runbook for manual evacuation are published and linked from the ticket.
implementation_steps: Design policy model: extend fleet metadata with residency tags, reserved_rps, burst_credits, and soft_evacuate_window. (API + DB migration)
Routing engine: add residency constraint evaluation and throughput-guard enforcement layer that consults reservations before placing new sessions.
Evacuation flow: implement soft-evacuate API which marks zone as draining, triggers pre-warm calls to surviving nodes, and enforces staged placement throttles.
Simulation harness: build a load-replay harness that runs synthetic traffic with residency tags, collects loss/latency, and pushes to our dashboard.
Telemetry & alerts: emit events for reservation saturation, evacuation progress, and policy violations; add alert thresholds for SRE.
E2E tests: integration tests that simulate zone loss, planned drain, and residency routing fallbacks; include regression tests for strict residency customers.
Console UX: add per-fleet controls for reservations and soft-evacuation and display active drains and reservation usage.
Canary: staged rollout to internal dedicated clusters, followed by opt-in customer pilot and then gradual enablement by region.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive pre-warming reduces cold-start latency but temporarily increases cost. We choose a conservative default (120s) and expose knob to customers.
Decision: residency routing will be a hard constraint for 'strict' tag; for 'preferred' tag we'll allow fallback with audit log (product decision approved by PM).
Open: policy conflict resolution when two fleets claim same reserved capacity in a single zone — we will enforce deterministic priority by reservation timestamp for this release.
SRE input: recommend configuring 20-25% cross-zone spare capacity for fleets with high throughput reservations to meet SLOs during single-zone evacuations.
Security: no plaintext residency metadata in customer requests; tags derived from customer account configuration and validated at the control plane.
timeline: Week 1: API+DB model + design review with PM/SEC/SRE
Week 2: Routing engine and evacuation flow implementation + unit tests
Week 3: Simulation harness + telemetry + integration tests
Week 4: Console UI, docs, internal canary, and pilot with two customers
Week 5: Rollout and post-deployment SLO verification
